end.summary:
Practised levels of organisation: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.
Gave examples for human and plant levels; 2 unaided examples were correct.
Explained that an organ is one body part, while an organ system is a group of organs working together.
Ordered the levels with some prompting; the organ/organism mix-up was corrected later in the lesson.
Teach-back was not completed successfully.
end.parentNote: Yash practised distinguishing an organ, such as the heart, from an organ system, such as the circulatory system, using the idea of connected parts working together. They also used a building-and-bricks analogy to organise the levels. There was a mix-up about whether organs and organisms could come in any order, and this was corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask Yash to arrange the five levels and give one human and one plant example for each.
